title: Increased eating in rats deprived of running1
notes: Empirical study arranged deprivation/removal of access to running and measured compensatory eating; canonical vocabulary has no response-deprivation process label, so coded as motivating/deprivation principles.

title: Immobility as an avoidance response, and its disruption by drugs1
notes: Escape-avoidance training established immobility as an avoidance response under shock; drug effects were secondary to the behavioral preparation.

title: A titration schedule on a treadmill
notes: Method measures treadmill performance decrement under heavy exertion; title/abstract do not map cleanly to a canonical behavioral process beyond effort/rate measures.

title: A well-regulated DC power supply
notes: Equipment note rather than an empirical behavioral study.

title: Errorless transfer of a discrimination across two continua1
notes: Arranged errorless discrimination transfer by superimposing and fading stimuli across color and line-orientation continua.

title: A technique for self-injection of drugs in the study of reinforcement1
notes: Technique/apparatus report with no abstracted empirical arrangement to code.

title: Control of the operate and release time of relays
notes: Instrumentation note rather than an empirical behavioral study.

title: Interresponse time as a function of continuous variables: a new method and some data1
processes: Schedule: Differential Reinforcement of Low Rates
notes: Method paper includes pigeon data under VI, FR, DRL, extinction, and stimulus generalization tests, with IRT and response-rate measurement central.

title: Response strength of an operant under stimulus control with satiated subjects
notes: Behavioral title suggests stimulus control with satiation, but no abstract is available to identify the arranged process confidently.

title: On the use of the squirrel monkey in behavorial and pharmacological experiments
notes: Husbandry/handling/drug-administration techniques for an experimental species, not an empirical behavioral-process article.

title: Concurrent performances: reinforcement interaction and response independence1
notes: Pigeons responded on two independent concurrent VI schedules; article analyzes matching, reinforcement-rate interaction, and response-rate independence.

title: Errata
notes: Erratum, not an empirical article.

title: Behavioral effects of pairing an SD with a decreasing limited-hold reinforcement schedule
notes: Multiple schedule arranged limited-hold reinforcement components with and without discriminative stimuli while reducing temporal parameters.

title: An automatic paper folder1
notes: Apparatus/instrumentation note rather than an empirical behavioral study.

title: A sequential response method of studying complex behavior in animals and its application to the measurement of drug effects1
notes: Rats were shaped to perform specified response sequences, then drug effects were assessed as a function of sequence complexity.

title: An improved live-worm dispenser1
notes: Apparatus note rather than an empirical behavioral article.

title: The effects of drl schedules on some characteristics of word utterance1
processes: Schedule: Differential Reinforcement of Low Rates
notes: Selected verbal responses were shaped and reinforced under DRL schedules; intervening verbal chains and IRT distributions were analyzed.

title: A multi-purpose perceptual device1
notes: Device/method note with no empirical behavioral arrangement available to code.

title: Effects of chlorpromazine and d-amphetamine on escape and avoidance behavior under a temporally defined schedule of negative reinforcement1
notes: Rats responded under temporally defined negative reinforcement producing escape-like and avoidance-like behavior; drug effects were measured against that baseline.

title: An apparatus for delivering pain shock to monkeys1
notes: Shock-delivery apparatus note rather than an empirical behavioral article.

title: Concurrent performances: a baseline for the study of reinforcement magnitude1
notes: Compared single-key VI and concurrent independent VI schedules while varying reinforcement duration as magnitude.

title: General activity as instrumental: application to avoidance training1
notes: Sidman avoidance in pigeons was used to demonstrate minimally restricted instrumental response form, warning-signal effects, and discrimination reversal.

title: Amplitude-induction gradient of a small-scale (covert) operant1
notes: A covert thumb-contraction amplitude subclass was reinforced with money-mediated feedback, shifting the response-amplitude distribution; extinction restored the prior skew.

title: Recording responding in the undergraduate laboratory course
notes: Instructional/laboratory recording-method note with no empirical behavioral arrangement to code.

title: Fixed-interval performances with added stimuli in monkeys1
notes: Monkeys responded on fixed-interval schedules with visual, auditory, and combined clock stimuli plus a limited-hold contingency.

title: A fixed interval schedule in which the interval is initiated by a response
notes: Two-bar FI procedure required a response to initiate each interval and separated post-reinforcement and fixed-interval pauses for measurement.

title: Behavioral effects of caffeine, methamphetamine, and methylphenidate in the rat
notes: Empirical drug study used fixed-interval and fixed-number food-reinforcement procedures; fixed-number likely maps to fixed-ratio, but human review should confirm.

title: Some effects of combined SDs1
notes: Combined discriminative stimuli from a multiple schedule summated their control over responding.

title: A device permitting the use of shock with contact relays1
notes: Apparatus/electronics note rather than an empirical behavioral article.

title: Intermittent punishment of SΔ responding in matching to sample1
notes: Incorrect matching responses were followed by continuous or FR-scheduled time-out; accuracy varied with time-out duration and frequency.

title: Free-operant avoidance conditioning in individual and paired human subjects1
notes: Humans acquired button-press avoidance under a nondiscriminated free-operant shock-shock/response-shock avoidance regimen.

title: Two parameters of a temporally defined schedule of negative reinforcement
notes: Parametric study of temporally defined negative reinforcement schedules that generated escape or avoidance behavior at different values.

title: Experimental self-punishment and superstitious escape behavior
notes: Rats were trained to escape shock, then bar holding was punished; inescapable shocks also sustained response patterns interpreted as superstitious escape.

title: Effects of increment size and reinforcer volume on progressive ratio performance1
notes: Progressive-ratio responding was examined across ratio increment size and liquid reinforcer volume, including satiation effects at larger volumes.

title: A method for rapid conditioning of stable avoidance bar pressing behavior1
notes: Title indicates avoidance conditioning but no abstract is available to identify whether the specific arranged procedure maps to discriminated avoidance or another canonical process.

title: d-Amphetamine-chlorpromazine antagonism in a food reinforced operant1
notes: Rats responded on a milk-reinforced FR 10 baseline while drug antagonism effects on responding were measured.

title: Elimination of behavior of mental patients by response-produced extinction1
notes: After conditioning high-rate responding, response-produced timeout/extinction eliminated behavior when an alternative reinforced response maintained overall reinforcement.

title: A manipulandum for use with rats responding to auditory stimuli
notes: Manipulandum/device note rather than an empirical behavioral article.

title: Response cost and the aversive control of human operant behavior1
notes: Human avoidance, escape, and avoidance-escape behavior were studied under point-loss response-cost conditions.

title: A pulser circuit for relay programming
notes: Electronics/programming apparatus note rather than an empirical behavioral article.
